title: Southwest Egg Bake
subtitle: Peppers, salsa, and pepper jack in a crew-sized egg bake.
description: Pepper jack, salsa, and bell peppers baked into a Southwest egg casserole — slice, serve, and pass the hot sauce.

ingredients.name: turkey sausage or lean pork sausage
baby spinach
ingredients.notes: or chopped kale, sautéed and squeezed dry

ingredients.name: loaf day-old bread
ingredients.notes: cubed (optional), turns it into a strata

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Southwest Egg Bake in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan. If using bread cubes, toast them 6–8 minutes so the bake doesn’t go soggy. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the pan
steps.instruction: Spread sausage, onion, and spinach in the pan. Add half the cheese. (If using bread cubes, fold them through now.) Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Egg mix
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs with milk, salt, pepper, and a pinch of paprika. Pour evenly. Top with remaining cheese. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Bake to set
steps.instruction: Bake until the center is set and the edges are browned. If it jiggles like loose custard, give it 5 more minutes. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 35 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest for clean slices
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes so slices hold for the line. Cut into squares; hold warm covered. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
